title: Architecture Review & Refactoring
outcome: Review and refactor TaskFlow architecture using evidence: dependency direction, duplication, tests, complexity, security, and operational boundaries.
artifact: Architecture review report plus one behavior-preserving refactor backed by tests and an ADR.
labSteps: Draw the current dependency graph from UI to database and mark places responsibilities leak across boundaries.
Find one duplication or accidental abstraction whose cost is visible in real code.
Create/strengthen tests around the behavior before moving code.
Refactor in small commits, verifying typecheck/tests after each conceptual move.
Measure whether the result reduced coupling/duplication or merely moved files.
Write a short ADR recording context, decision, alternatives, consequences, and when to revisit.
failureModes: Refactor with no behavioral safety net
Adding layers because they look enterprise
Confusing folder count with architecture quality
mastery: Can identify architectural smell with evidence
Can document tradeoffs in an ADR
principles: Refactoring should improve boundaries and clarity while preserving externally observable behavior.
Use tests and architecture checks as safety nets before moving responsibilities across modules.
Remove abstractions that no longer earn their complexity instead of only adding new layers.
Document significant architectural decisions so future maintainers understand the trade-offs that shaped the system.
